#376 implement.summary:
#376 is fixed in one commit on branch fix/376-continue-restores-the-session-model in /tmp/wt-376, on top of 8f7d98aa. It is not pushed. When a session that already has a conversation is reopened and the user named no model, aelix now puts it back on the model it last ran on. 'Named a model' means --model, --provider or --api-key on the command line, or an agent profile with model: or provider:. The restore happens in one place, the model resolve inside _build_harness_options. It runs after providers registered by extensions in setup() are bound, and before the thinking level is clamped to the model. That one place covers startup --continue/--resume/--session/--fork, the in-session /resume, /fork, /import and /reload, and RPC switch_session. /new is an empty session, so it starts on the launch model, as in pi.

How the model is found: the same rule as pi's getBranchSelection, in the new helper session.context.resolve_resumed_model. Walking back from the end of the session, the first model_change entry or the first assistant message that names its provider and model wins. aelix never writes a model_change for the model a session was launched on, so for most sessions the assistant messages are the only record. An assistant message without those names, such as a refused turn, is skipped.

When the recorded model may come back (runtime_bootstrap.restore_session_route, exact provider and id, none of the launch's guessing):
- A model in the catalogue, models.json or an extension comes back if its provider has a key from any source, a project .env included. This matches pi and matches --provider.
- An id no catalogue lists comes back only on a provider the user defined, or on the user's own key (not a .env). This is the same condition the launch uses before sending an uncatalogued id to OpenRouter.

Otherwise the run uses what it would have picked without the session and prints pi's line: 'Could not restore model P/ID. Using P2/ID2'. The 'Using' half appears only if that fallback can run. The TUI shows the line under the banner and after /resume, /import, /fork and /clone. -p, --mode json and RPC print it on stderr.

Related changes:
- The -p/json 'no model selected' check now looks at the restored model, not the settings default.
- A rebuild that restored the session's model is no longer put on hold by the #367 late-provider rule, because that rule is about where the launch flags and settings would land.
- An RPC prompt on a model that cannot run is now refused before it is accepted (success: false) and nothing is written to the session.
- The harness's mid-turn set_model wrote the protocol name (e.g. anthropic-messages) into model_change's provider field. It now writes the provider.

Docs: ADR-0239 has a dated amendment (its decision 7, 'the model is not restored here', is superseded), ADR-0250 §2.11 has a note about the hold, both index rows are updated, the providers-and-models and getting-started guides plus their bundled copies are updated, and CHANGELOG Fixed has an entry. The #289 argv routing and #286 defaultThinkingLevel seed are untouched. The cli/entry.py lines changed are listed in the commit message. The real-model driver is /Users/handochan/dev/aelix-ai/.omc/probes/376-live/impl/drive.py (with mock_anthropic.py). It takes the provider and model as arguments, uses a mock with fake keys, or a real key via --key-env, and its header gives an OpenRouter example command.

owner_decisions: A .env key can restore a catalogued session model, the same as pi's hasConfiguredAuth and as --provider. An uncatalogued id needs the user's own key (the guard-2 condition). A stricter owner might require the user's own key in both cases, but then sessions of users who keep keys only in a project .env would never restore.

The fallback is what aelix's launch would pick (settings default or nothing). It is not pi's findInitialModel, which also takes the first available model. With nothing runnable, the line reads 'Could not restore model P/ID' plus the existing gate messages, instead of pi's 'No models available'.
The fallback line goes to stderr in -p, json and RPC. pi prints it only in interactive mode.
The line is pi's exact text and gives no reason. Adding '(no key)' or '(model gone)' would help users.
--api-key counts as naming a model, so it disables the restore.

/reload now restores the session's recorded model instead of re-resolving the launch flags and settings. This is closer to pi, where reload keeps the live model. One result: a /model pick of a provider registered during session_start is no longer held after /reload once that model has answered.
The RPC prompt refusal changes the RPC contract for clients that used to get success:true followed by an error event on a placeholder model.
follow_ups: set_model still writes no model_change when idle (the turn-phase gate that ADR-0239 decision 7 named). A /model pick followed by a quit before any prompt is not restored. Fixing it needs care: the late-hold apply() calls set_model with a placeholder and would record it.
/agents use with a profile that names no model re-resolves the launch flags and settings. In a restored session it moves off the restored model. Decide whether it should keep the live model.

A prompt on a provider with no key is still written to the session before failing in -p and the TUI. The base H run showed 'No API key for provider' with messages appended. pi checks auth before recording the message (agent-session.ts:2037-2050).
Sessions do not record their launch model as a model_change, as pi does (sdk.ts:452-455). Assistant responses cover it today, but a session whose only answers failed with no provenance has no record.

The real-model resume check (CLAUDE.md rule 10) is still pending for the main loop: .omc/probes/376-live/impl/drive.py with --key-env and no --mock-port. Phases ABCDEFTRG; --long controls how many tokens phase A spends.

blocking.title: An idle /model pick is lost when the session is reopened (regression vs 8f7d98aa, diverges from pi)
blocking.detail: Idle AgentHarness.set_model writes no model_change; only the in-turn path does. The TUI picker and /model <arg> call it while idle. The restore now reads the session record ahead of the settings default. So /model X followed by a quit with no prompt, then aelix --continue, comes back on the older model. On the parent the pick came back, because the picker persists the settings default. pi's setModel always appends model_change (agent-session.ts:2485). /clone and /reload after an idle pick also land on the old record. The parent also dropped the pick there, but on the launch model instead. The sweep listed only the in-turn set_model. ADR-0239 records the quit case as a divergence, but nowhere says it regressed from the parent. Fix: write model_change on an idle set_model, as #198 did for the thinking level.

blocking.title: A prompt that cannot run (no key) is still accepted and written; the 'Using' half names a keyless fallback
blocking.detail: The RPC gate checks only is_runnable (adapter). pi's prompt, at the very lines the commit cites (agent-session.ts:2032-2050), also refuses a model without auth before recording. Reachable on a resume: the session's model has no key, so the restore fails, and the settings default it falls back to has no key either. The prompt is accepted (success true), the user message is written, and the turn fails. The failed turn's assistant message then names the keyless model, so it becomes the session's record. The next run says 'Could not restore model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5. Using anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5'. This falsifies the commit subject ('a prompt that cannot run is no longer written into it'), ADR-0239 decision 6 ('A prompt that cannot run writes nothing'), and the guide and ADR line that the 'Using' half appears 'only when the fallback can run'. pi's findInitialModel only falls back to models with auth.

Using anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5'; prompt success=True; file lines 8->10; user msg written=True; mock NONE. H2 (-p --continue): 'Warning: Could not restore model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5. Using anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5' then 'No API key found for Anthropic.' exit 1.

blocking.title: False documentation claims
blocking.detail: (a) The CHANGELOG says 'A model id no catalogue lists comes back only on a key of your own, never one from a project .env'. That is false for a models.json provider: restore_session_route takes _configured_auth (.env counts) for user-defined providers. The guide qualifies the claim ('one the launch sent to OpenRouter'); the CHANGELOG does not. (b) The guide and CHANGELOG say the restored model is 'the last /model pick the session recorded, or else the model that wrote its last answer'. A user's idle /model pick is never recorded, and the rule is whichever record is latest, not pick-first. (c) The guide puts RPC switch_session and /reload among the paths that 'say so', 'on stderr in ... RPC'. RPC switch_session falls back silently, and the TUI shows nothing after /reload (_commit_model_fallback is not called there). ADR decision 5 is accurate ('once at startup').
blocking.evidence: run-head-X.out: models.json localbox (apiKey LOCALBOX_API_KEY, models [listed-model]) + cwd .env only: X2 '--continue state localbox/unlisted-model', request reached mock on the .env key. run-head-ABGHS.out S: switch_session to an unrestorable session -> 'after anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 ... stderr='''. shell.py: _commit_model_fallback only at 1104, 1137, 3250.
